# es-foral-corporate-tax: figure and rule ledger
Frozen Guide SHA256 `226cfd82b2881c87b8989eceec3f0398fe4757967692f96f75dca01658d19929`; HEAD0b5e62451de50220ac6d80c7813d547d08108641. Writer evidence, not independent review or accountant attestation. Source quotations retain original language with whitespace joined; case figures are computed, not quoted statutory amounts. All source bodies are reused by exact identity, not silently replaced.
| # | Guide section and native LF | Figure / rule as written | Source act/article | Official URL | Exact short source quote | Actual read date | Type / scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who this applies to; LF28 | For 2026, the agreements use the EUR 12 million preceding-period operations threshold. Annualise operations for a short period and use estimated first-year operations until actual figures are known. Operations means VAT-exclusive consideration for business supplies, excluding the equivalence surcharge; it is not automatically accounting turnover or assets. At or below EUR 12 million, the ordinary single company pays the administration of its fiscal domicile. Above it, collection follows the current year's territorial operations, with the percentage rounded to two decimals. Calculate one company's taxable income under the selected governing law, then allocate its liability. Do not apply each territory's headline rate separately to its sales. [CE arts.14–18; CN arts.18–23.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Own Basque corporate law article 15 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969#a15 | Uno. Corresponderá de forma exclusiva a las Diputaciones Forales la exacción del Impuesto sobre Sociedades de los sujetos pasivos que tengan su domicilio fiscal en el País Vasco y su volumen de operaciones en el ejercicio anterior no hubiere excedido de 12 millones de euros. | 2026-10-28 | rule |
| 2 | Who this applies to; LF28 | For 2026, the agreements use the EUR 12 million preceding-period operations threshold. Annualise operations for a short period and use estimated first-year operations until actual figures are known. Operations means VAT-exclusive consideration for business supplies, excluding the equivalence surcharge; it is not automatically accounting turnover or assets. At or below EUR 12 million, the ordinary single company pays the administration of its fiscal domicile. Above it, collection follows the current year's territorial operations, with the percentage rounded to two decimals. Calculate one company's taxable income under the selected governing law, then allocate its liability. Do not apply each territory's headline rate separately to its sales. [CE arts.14–18; CN arts.18–23.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Own Basque corporate law article 15 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969#a15 | La proporción del volumen de operaciones realizada en cada territorio durante el ejercicio se determinará por aplicación de las reglas que se establecen en el artículo siguiente y se expresará en porcentaje redondeado con dos decimales. | 2026-10-28 | rule |
| 3 | Who this applies to; LF30 | For a Basque-domiciled company, Basque law governs unless preceding operations exceed EUR 12 million and at least 75% took place in common territory. A common-territory company above EUR 12 million uses Basque law if at least 75% of preceding operations took place in the Basque Country; a common-domiciled fiscal-group member needs 100% there. Select the province under that province's art.2: domicile normally controls; if all Basque operations occurred outside the domicile province, use the sole operating province or the province with the larger share of the other two; a common-territory company coming into Basque law uses the province with the largest Basque operations share. Record all three provincial percentages, the common-territory percentage and preceding/current years separately. [CE art.14; B/A/G art.2.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Bizkaia NF11/2013](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54) | Own Basque corporate law article 14 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969#a14 | No obstante, los sujetos pasivos cuyo volumen de operaciones en el ejercicio anterior hubiera excedido de 12 millones de euros, y en dicho ejercicio hubieran realizado en territorio común el 75 por ciento o más de su volumen de operaciones, quedarán sometidos a la normativa de dicho territorio. | 2026-10-28 | rule |
| 4 | Who this applies to; LF34 | Build the operations ledger from the statutory connecting factors: goods generally where made available or where dispatch starts; transformed goods at the final transformation; industrial installations use the preparation/manufacturing place if installation cost does not exceed 15%; electricity at generating plants; immovable supplies and related services where the property is; ordinary services where performed from. Agriculture/fishing products, transport and leasing transport equipment have domicile rules; allocate foreign operations proportionately to the remaining operations. Customer address alone does not supply this analysis. [CE art.16; CN arts.20–21.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Own Basque corporate law article 16 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969#a16 | b) Si se trata de entregas con instalación de elementos industriales fuera del País Vasco, se entenderán realizadas en territorio vasco si los trabajos de preparación y fabricación se efectúan en dicho territorio y el coste de la instalación o montaje no excede del 15 por 100 del total de la contraprestación. | 2026-10-28 | rule |
| 5 | Who this applies to; LF36 | Advance payments use the last return's allocation, subject to the agreement's change-notification routes; deduct the instalment actually paid to each administration from its share. File with every administration entitled to collection. The governing law determines the instalment method even where another administration collects part of it. A State-law company allocating tax to a foral treasury must therefore retain State instalment calculations. [CE arts.17–18; CN arts.22–24.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Own Basque corporate law article 17 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969#a17 | Dos. Los sujetos pasivos que deban tributar a ambas Administraciones ingresarán el pago fraccionado del impuesto en proporción al volumen de operaciones realizado en cada territorio. A estos efectos, se aplicará la proporción determinada en la última declaración-liquidación del Impuesto. | 2026-10-28 | rule |

| 8 | Who this applies to; LF32 | For Navarra, exclusive Navarra collection entails Navarra law. A company paying both Navarra and the State uses domicile law, except a Navarra-domiciled company with at least 75% preceding operations in common territory uses common law; a common-domiciled company with at least 75% in Navarra uses Navarra law, with the art.18 fiscal-group exception. Keep a case involving both Navarra and one or more Basque provinces for a specific agreement analysis rather than treating Navarra as a fourth Basque province. [CN arts.18–19.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Navarra Economic Agreement own allocation | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117#a1-21 | 2. | 127 | The base / Taxable-base reconciliation; LF82 | Sources: [B/A/G arts.25 bis,31–35; N arts.23–24,35–36](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54), [Navarra LF26/2016](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-2356). The Basque financing rules exclude, among others, qualifying standalone companies with no related entities/foreign PE, credit/insurance entities and final extinction outside restructuring, and contain group-equity and acquisition-debt rules. Navarra's exemption list differs. | 135 | The base / Basque domestic-dividend fallback; LF86 | In Bizkaia, Álava and Gipuzkoa, failing the full article 33.1 participation-exemption conditions does not automatically make a dividend fully taxable. | 163 | The base / Ordinary receivable impairment; LF103 | The Basque article 22.2 exclusions cover public-body debts/guarantees, bank or mutual-guarantee cover, real security/title-retention/retention rights, credit insurance and expressly renewed or extended debts, with the stated exception for arbitration or litigation over the debt's existence or amount and the stated lost/impaired-security exception. Related-party impairments require judicially declared insolvency. Navarra article 20.1.2º has its own exclusions: public-body debts, public/bank/mutual guarantees and credit insurance (to the covered amount), real security except lost/impaired security, and express renewal/extension; apply its specified judicial/arbitral exception rather than assuming that six months overrides a guarantee. | 220 | The base / Passenger-vehicle expense computation; LF129 | Gipuzkoa art.31.3.a/b has the same 50%/100%, EUR 3,000/6,000, EUR 30,000 and electric EUR 4,000/8,000/EUR 40,000 depreciation comparators and EUR 3,600/7,200 other-cost ceilings, but its own disposal-loss/monetary-correction method. Its statute does not separately reproduce the Bizkaia/Álava proportionate-financing formula in those clauses. Preserve that difference rather than inserting it by analogy. | 278 | The base / Depreciation and goodwill; LF150 | Basque micro/small companies can freely depreciate qualifying new tangible assets excluding buildings and specified passenger vehicles; unit-cost assets at most EUR 1,500 have a separate free-depreciation route. Medium companies can multiply the normal maximum by 1.5 for qualifying new assets. Microcompanies can elect a 25%-of-opening-net-tax-value pool over the eligible asset population, replacing accounting depreciation/impairment and retaining the election while micro status continues; that pooling excludes the art.21.1 free-depreciation methods. Bizkaia/Álava art21 provide their specified EUR20,000/EUR40,000 total-deduction limits. Gipuzkoa art21.1(g)/(h)/21.4 instead uses its own qualifying vehicle/charging and art31 restrictions; do not import the Bizkaia/Álava EUR20,000 total cap into that separate route. Navarra small companies use 1.5 times the normal maximum for qualifying new tangible assets and new investment property, with the construction/delivery conditions in art.16.7. Its separate free-depreciation cases include tangible assets of unit cost at most EUR 1,800 and exclusive permanent R&D assets/capitalised R&D, plus the conditional early-year labour-company and priority-agricultural cases; art.18.4 excludes combining its free depreciation with other tax incentives except art.61 R&D credit. [B/A/G art.21; N arts.16–18.](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54), [Navarra LF26/2016](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-2356) | Own Basque corporate law article 21 | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887#a21 | a) Los elementos del inmovilizado material e intangible cuyo valor unitario no exceda de 1.500 euros, cualquiera que sea la fecha de adquisición de los mismos. | 2026-10-28 | rule |

| 303 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF262 | The separate women/under-36 indefinite-hire method is B art.66 decies and A/G art.66 octies. For contracts formalised in 2026 the emergency instruments raise the salary percentage from 35% to **45%**, retaining the annual-SMI credit cap. | 342 | The base / Micro deduction and reserves; LF168 | The Basque productive/business reserve in art.53 provides a separate local reserve/materialisation method. Álava's current rates are a 65%-of-dotations reduction capped at 45% of taxable base and a 50%-of-fiscal-equity reserve balance, with the three-year investment categories, double-investment requirement for new art.61 assets and prior approval for the specified participation route. Bizkaia also uses 65%/45%/50%; Gipuzkoa uses 60%/45%/50% with its expressly pre-corrections/pre-loss base ceiling. The local business-angel route has its own eligibility and EUR 100,000-per-project ceiling; participation investments ordinarily require five-year retention, and the specified industrial-project participation route requires prior administrative approval. The three-year materialisation failure reverses the corresponding reduction with its separate 15% uplift; unlawful disposal has the separate 5%-per-year rule. Do not combine the micro 15% option with these reserves or claim a credit on the same investment used to materialise an incompatible reserve. [A art.53; B/G arts.32.4,53,67.6.](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Bizkaia NF11/2013](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54) | Own Basque corporate law article 53 | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887#a53 | 1. | 452 | The base / Basque ordinary calculation; LF219 | For **Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa**, regulation article 33 bis expressly separates the article 59.4 investment test from full entitlement to the corresponding articles 61–65 credit. Making an investment of a type described in those articles can satisfy the investment limb even where the conditions required to claim that credit are not fulfilled. Test the investment and workforce limbs independently, and calculate any generated credit separately. For example, assume an ordinary 24% company with no staff-maintenance/increase limb, positive base EUR 100,000, and EUR 5,000 of new business machinery of an article 61 asset type. If preceding net qualifying assets are EUR 100,000 and there are no other investments, EUR 5,000 fails the over-10%-or-over-EUR-5m article 61.3(d) credit threshold, so this investment generates no article 61 credit. It can nevertheless establish the article 59.4 investment limb under B/G regulation article 33 bis: the applicable ordinary-credit floor is EUR 17,000 rather than EUR 19,000. With a separately eligible EUR 6,000 ordinary-bucket credit, gross quota EUR 24,000 and bucket capacity EUR 8,400, a EUR 6,000 claim leaves EUR 18,000 and satisfies the 17% floor. This illustration creates no credit on the EUR 5,000 investment. An enacted Álava equivalent to the broader B/G33bis deeming rule has not been established; the narrow own-statutory amount-threshold method below does not assume one. Sources: B/G article 59.4, article 61.3(d), and BR/GR article 33 bis in the laws/regulations linked in Sources. | Own Basque corporate law article 33bis | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_203_2013.pdf/5d2f80fc-9d5b-0f71-b578-56da0a5a0c50?t=1679483614806#a33bis | A los efectos de lo dispuesto en el apartado 4 del artículo 59 de la Norma Foral del impuesto se entenderá que se realizan inversiones susceptibles de generar las deducciones establecidas en los artículos 61 a 65 de dicha Norma Foral cuando se realice cualquiera de las inversiones contempladas en dichos artículos, sin que sea necesario que se cumplan los requisitos necesarios para acreditar el derecho a aplicar las deducciones señaladas. | 2026-10-28 | rule |

| 454 | The base / Álava: the ordinary amount-threshold investment case; LF223 | **Source-derived interpretation, limited to the amount gate.** Álava article 59.4 tests whether an actual investment is capable of generating an article 61–65 credit, separately from calculating and using that credit. For an ordinary company taxed at the general 24% rate, an otherwise qualifying new business machine meets that investment limb where the **only** failed credit-generation condition is article 61.3(d)'s aggregate amount threshold. This is the identified interpretation of Álava's own potential-investment wording and article 61.1/3, not a B/G article 33 bis transplant or an express enacted Álava deeming rule. Its own article 53.2 and operative regulation article 32 bis expressly require actual-credit eligibility and all conditions for the separate productive reserve; that different test is not imported into article 59.4. Do not extend this amount-only method to a private, nonbusiness, used, land, unproved or otherwise unsuitable asset. | 457 | The base / Álava: the ordinary amount-threshold investment case; LF225 | Assume taxable base EUR 100,000, unadjusted liquid quota EUR 24,000, current indefinite staff 1 against prior 2, no staff increase, no complementary-tax exclusion, no surcharge or other quota adjustment, no minimum-exempt credit and no five-period block election. A new business machine costing EUR 5,000 meets the other article 61 asset conditions. Relevant prior net assets of EUR 100,000 and no other investment make it fail the strictly-over-10%-or-over-EUR-5m credit threshold. Generated article 61 credit is zero. Under the stated source-derived investment interpretation, the floor is EUR 17,000 instead of EUR 19,000. A separately entitled, unexpired EUR 6,000 ordinary-bucket credit fits the EUR 8,400 article 67 capacity and leaves EUR 18,000; without the investment limb only EUR 5,000 could be used and EUR 1,000 would carry. With a separately entitled EUR 8,000 credit, use EUR 7,000 and carry EUR 1,000. The machine itself creates no EUR 500 credit. With no separate credit, quota remains EUR 24,000: 17% is a credit-use floor, not the ordinary tax rate or a cash refund. | 470 | The base / Investment, research and employment; LF243 | The Basque art.67.3 general credit base excludes interest, indirect taxes/surcharges, construction margin, tendering technical costs, dismantling/removal costs and land. Cap it at market value, require accounting recognition and ordinarily subtract the grant amount multiplied by (100% minus the company's rate). Apply express special overrides: Álava/Gipuzkoa art.65.3 environmental credits and the applicable bicycle provisions subtract grants in full. Bizkaia art.65 does not contain that environmental subsidy override, so its ordinary art.67.3 reduction is the grant multiplied by (100% minus the company's tax rate). Álava art.62.3 expressly overrides art.67 for the funded investments within its R&D base. B/G art.64 and A art.64 also exclude listed travel, training, project-documentation/management-certification, administration and overhead costs from R&D/innovation bases. Investment credits normally arise on commissioning; the long-order payment election has the one-month contract-notification requirement. Maintain eligible assets for five years, or three for movables, unless useful life is shorter, with the specified three-month replacement exception; earlier disqualification recovers the credit plus interest. Navarra chapter-III bases instead subtract grants in full under art.67.2 and use its own retention/time rules. | 528 | The base / Investment, research and employment; LF258 | Navarra declared-social-interest sponsorship credits are marginal 30% throughEUR 30,000,35% on the nextEUR 30,000 and 40% above EUR 60,000, with 40% on qualifying women-only sport sponsorship, recipient reporting and the gambling exclusion. Renewable-energy investment starts at 15%, with uplifts capped at 30%: ten points for zero-GHG electricity generation, ten for qualifying storage over2kWh, five for a microgrid with two renewable sources, five for shared self-consumption/energy communities; thermal hydraulic heating/hot-water connection adds five points and replacing gas with renewable hydrogen adds up to fifteen according to the qualifying use. Apply the mandatory-building-installation exclusions, special70%-of-cost mixed hot-water/heating rule and heat-pump renewable-share calculation, supported by the energy-authority report; new qualifying electric vehicles 30%, plug-in hybrids 5%, with category base capsEUR 35,000(M1/N1), EUR 5,000(L1e/L2e), EUR 10,000(L3e/L4e/L5e), EUR 15,000(L6e/L7e), EUR 150,000(N 2/N 3). The excess over the relevant vehicle/charger base cap can qualify separately under art.58, avoiding duplicate base. The new 2026 decarbonisation credit is 15% of qualifying new tangible business investment achieving at least 30,000 kWh/year final-energy savings, less the amount received for transferring the energy savings; cap the credit at EUR 1.5m. Generation follows the resolution registering the energy-saving certificates, supported by the competent energy authority's report. Keep art.64 investments separately identified as fixed assets for five years or shorter useful life and apply the statutory leasing, retention and clawback conditions. Separate these from real-estate energy improvements and from the personal income-tax vehicle credit. The new 2026 decarbonisation credit is 15% of qualifying new tangible business investment achieving at least 30,000 kWh/year final-energy savings, less the amount received for transferring the energy savings; cap the credit at EUR 1.5m. Generation follows the resolution registering the energy-saving certificates, supported by the competent energy authority's report. Keep art.64 investments separately identified as fixed assets for five years or shorter useful life and apply the statutory leasing, retention and clawback conditions. Separate these from real-estate energy improvements and from the personal income-tax vehicle credit. | 547 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF264 | All three provinces provide a new conciliation-plan credit: 5% of liquid quota in the introduction year capped EUR 2,500; 15% in the first year at least one third of staff use a qualifying measure capped EUR 7,500. Micro/small companies increase the two percentages by five points to 10%/20%, retaining those caps. | 559 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF266 | Preferred EPSV employer contributions under collective bargaining generate 15% credit when imputed contributions are at least 1.5% but below 2.5% of annual gross pay, 20% from 2.5% to below 4%, and 25% at least 4% or for the specified under-36 employee contributions. Other eligible employment social-provision systems generate 10% where contributions reach at least 1.5% of annual gross pay or favour under-36 employees, including qualifying EU/EEA equivalents. Use the local regulatory annual-gross-pay denominator and the age-at-accrual provisions; the base is qualifying contributions actually imputed from collective bargaining. These permanent methods apply in 2026; the larger credits expressly confined to 2025 do not. [B arts.66 septies/octies and DA 31–33; A arts.66 sexies/septies; G arts.66 quinquies/sexies and implementing regulations.](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54) | Own Basque corporate law article 66septies | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887#a66septies | a) Cuando las contribuciones empresariales realizadas e imputadas fiscalmente a las personas trabajadoras sean iguales o superiores al 1,5 por 100 e inferiores al 2,5 por 100 del salario bruto anual total en la entidad empleadora, el porcentaje de deducción será del 15 por 100. | 2026-10-28 | rule |

| 575 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF266 | Preferred EPSV employer contributions under collective bargaining generate 15% credit when imputed contributions are at least 1.5% but below 2.5% of annual gross pay, 20% from 2.5% to below 4%, and 25% at least 4% or for the specified under-36 employee contributions. Other eligible employment social-provision systems generate 10% where contributions reach at least 1.5% of annual gross pay or favour under-36 employees, including qualifying EU/EEA equivalents. Use the local regulatory annual-gross-pay denominator and the age-at-accrual provisions; the base is qualifying contributions actually imputed from collective bargaining. These permanent methods apply in 2026; the larger credits expressly confined to 2025 do not. | 602 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF274 | The environmental art.65 credit in each province is 35% for qualifying new renewable/hydrogen/renewable-fuel generation, consumption, distribution, clean-technology-list equipment, carbon capture for the named permitted destinations, and material recycling/circularity investments. The separate 15% branch covers approved contaminated-soil work and the named applied projects (energy recovery where material recovery is unavailable, voluntary ecosystem regeneration beyond compulsory measures, water saving/treatment, best/emerging techniques and eligible sustainable transport). Match the project to a statutory category, obtain the specified regional/provincial certification or reasoned report, apply Bizkaia's art.67.3 subsidy reduction or Álava/Gipuzkoa's express full-grant reduction in art.65.3, prevent incompatible category overlap and apply the 50%-of-residual-quota bucket/minimum exception. Bizkaia and Álava state a EUR 40,000 clean-list passenger-car base cap; Gipuzkoa excludes principal waste-management businesses from the named energy-recovery branch. Financed-credit transfers under art.65 bis need their own signed contract, certification, communication and recipient limit and do not let both project owner and financer claim the transferred amount. | 611 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF278 | Bizkaia and Álava art.66 bis give 25% of eligible new/recent SME-share investment, increased to 35% for the statutory innovative or silver-economy company category. Require an eligible unlisted company form, real new business and its people/assets, acquisition at formation or in the following five years (seven for the innovative route, with its high-initial-risk-financing exception), retention **longer than five years**, the issuing company's certificate and innovation evidence where relevant. For each slice record the taxable-base increment `I_j` actually derived from that profit, with its identifiable tax additions, exclusions, deductions and used losses. Apply the selected law's tax treatment to those facts; an unsupported allocation is not a verified input. For a constant general24% rate, the corresponding gross-quota portion is `q_j=24% × I_j` and the additional quota is `S=1%q1+2%q2+3%q3+4%q4`. Ordinary gross quota plus `S` is the increased gross quota. This is a source-derived computation, not a published provincial algebra ruling. Álava's own articles 15/31/56.7/57 also support the conditional quota step; the separate net-result worksheet below derives its own `R/M/I_j` from the stated fully taxable PGC/current-tax ledger rather than stipulating approved measurements. Other accounting and tax-adjustment populations remain bounded as stated there. Assume a standalone general24% trading company which fails the art.13 medium-company size tests, has been active for more than four periods, has no group/restart/exceptional-result issue, and has claimed none of its own regulation's excluded credits in any of the four periods. Each previous period has pre-tax profit80,000 and deductible depreciation20,000, giving own `R=100,000` and `M=100,000`. Current pre-tax profit190,000 plus deductible depreciation60,000 gives `R=250,000`; no impairment, income adjustment, reserve deduction, other tax difference, used loss or credit changes these figures. The actual operating-profit ledger establishes that the60,000 depreciation belongs to the continuing business and that the115,000 profit above `1.35M` consists of additional fully taxable income with no attributable expense or tax adjustment. Thus the underlying business at `R=135,000` has taxable profit75,000, and adding the four excess slices15,000/25,000/25,000/50,000 reconciles exactly to actual taxable base190,000. This is factual attribution of the excess, not a rule assigning every company's depreciation to its underlying business. Each previous period has pre-tax profit80,000 and deductible depreciation20,000, giving own `R=100,000` and `M=100,000`. Current pre-tax profit190,000 plus deductible depreciation60,000 gives `R=250,000`; no impairment, income adjustment, reserve deduction, other tax difference, used loss or credit changes these figures. The actual operating-profit ledger establishes that the60,000 depreciation belongs to the continuing business and that the115,000 profit above `1.35M` consists of additional fully taxable income with no attributable expense or tax adjustment. Thus the underlying business at `R=135,000` has taxable profit75,000, and adding the four excess slices15,000/25,000/25,000/50,000 reconciles exactly to actual taxable base190,000. This is factual attribution of the excess, not a rule assigning every company's depreciation to its underlying business. | 687 | The base / Extraordinary-profit surcharge2026–2030; LF313 | Ordinary gross quota is `190,000 ×24%=45,600`; increased gross quota is `45,600+816=46,416`. Assuming the only accounting tax expense is that current charge, net accounting profit143,584 plus nondeductible tax expense46,416 reconciles to pre-tax/taxable profit190,000, and adding depreciation60,000 recovers `R=250,000`. The surcharge is a quota increase, not a deduction from taxable income. All amounts here are exact whole euros; the example establishes no intermediate or return-field rounding convention. The816 result follows the stated ledger and own gross-quota wording. | 702 | The base / Álava: labelled ordinary net-result interpretation; LF325 | **Taxable excess and the tax-expense feedback.** At the first trigger, net result `1.35×M` corresponds to pre-tax/taxable profit `E0=1.35×M/(1−t)`, with no surcharge yet. If `E≤E0`, this worksheet produces no surcharge. Above that point, under this selected correspondence reading, use net-result band widths `0.15×M`, `0.25×M`, `0.25×M`, then an unlimited remainder, with additional quota percentages `a=1%,2%,3%,4%` respectively. For a taxable increment `I` in one band, the ordinary quota is `t×I`, its surcharge is `a×t×I`, and the resulting net-accounting increment is `I−t×I−a×t×I`. Thus a finite net-result band width `W` admits taxable increment `W/(1−t−a×t)`. Starting with the actual taxable profit above `E0`, fill those taxable capacities sequentially; call the admitted amounts `I1` through `I4`. Calculate `S=t×(0.01×I1+0.02×I2+0.03×I3+0.04×I4)`. Finally reconcile the resulting `R`, `Q` and `BI`. This expressly derives the taxable increase from the accounting excess and its own article 31 tax correction; merely applying 24% to net slices would omit that correction. | 760 | Cross-border points; LF377 | Sources: [B/A/G art.43; N art.30; BR/AR/GR related-party chapters; NR arts.18–19,29–32](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54), [Navarra LF26/2016](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-2356), [Bizkaia DF203/2013](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_203_2013.pdf/5d2f80fc-9d5b-0f71-b578-56da0a5a0c50?t=1679483614806), [Álava DF41/2014](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/indice-reglamento-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades-cas-5-pdf), [Gipuzkoa DF17/2015](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761381E7/DF%2017-2015%20%282026%29.pdf/ad233e14-7236-0450-948f-50a669df270f), [Navarra DF114/2017](https://www.navarra.es/documents/48192/6699806/Reglamento%20IS.pdf/ea37edba-eb1b-22d7-a04b-9f9d8fbba4e6). The Basque safe-threshold documentation routes for qualifying SME remuneration, financing and property rent have separate floor, prior-year comparison and regulatory conditions. For example, the remuneration floor is the maximum of EUR 36,000(EUR 60,000 medium), the comparable employee's pay and prior-two-year average; it requires actual monetary remuneration and proportionate part-time treatment. Financing uses the specified official one-year Euribor plus 2 points(or 5 if the related borrower is an individual), compares the prior two-year effective rate and resets after five years; property-rent valuation differs by local land-value system. These are documentation routes, not automatic substitution of an interest rate or salary for a proper arm's-length result. The detailed local declarations/evidence requirements must be met before claiming them. [B/A/G art.43.6–9 and corresponding regulations.](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54) | Own Basque corporate law article 43 | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887#a43 | - 36.000 ó 60.000 euros anuales, según se trate de microempresas y pequeñas empresas o de medianas empresas, para aquellas personas físicas vinculadas que tengan una dedicación a jornada completa, o la parte proporcional en caso contrario. | 2026-10-28 | rule |

The Basque safe-threshold documentation routes for qualifying SME remuneration, financing and property rent have separate floor, prior-year comparison and regulatory conditions. For example, the remuneration floor is the maximum of EUR 36,000(EUR 60,000 medium), the comparable employee's pay and prior-two-year average; it requires actual monetary remuneration and proportionate part-time treatment. The detailed local declarations/evidence requirements must be met before claiming them. The Basque safe-threshold documentation routes for qualifying SME remuneration, financing and property rent have separate floor, prior-year comparison and regulatory conditions. For example, the remuneration floor is the maximum of EUR 36,000(EUR 60,000 medium), the comparable employee's pay and prior-two-year average; it requires actual monetary remuneration and proportionate part-time treatment. Financing uses the specified official one-year Euribor plus 2 points(or 5 if the related borrower is an individual), compares the prior two-year effective rate and resets after five years; property-rent valuation differs by local land-value system. These are documentation routes, not automatic substitution of an interest rate or salary for a proper arm's-length result. The detailed local declarations/evidence requirements must be met before claiming them. | 825 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF268 | For tax periods **beginning from 1 January 2025 through 31 December 2029**, qualifying tax-imputed collective-bargaining contributions **below 1.5%** of the employer's annual gross pay generate a **10% credit for preferred EPSV plans** or **5% for other employment systems**. Apply articles 59 and 67, including the quota limits and the prohibition on claiming two chapter-III credits for the same expense. Keep the permanent under-36 treatment when applicable; do not add a transitional credit on the same contribution. A plan outside the preferred EPSV form, including an EU/EEA employment system, follows the preferred permanent bands and preferred 10% transitional route if its specifications satisfy the statutory preferred-plan requirements. Foreign location alone does not establish that equivalence. Sources: B DA 31–33, A DA 28–30 and G DA 26–28 in the current laws linked above. | Own transitional preferred pension DA | https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887 | Con efectos para los periodos impositivos iniciados entre el 1 de enero de 2025 y el 31 de diciembre de 2029 las contribuciones realizadas a Planes de Previsión Social Preferentes a que se refiere el artículo 66 septies que hayan sido imputadas fiscalmente a las personas trabajadoras y derivadas de la negociación colectiva darán derecho a una deducción en la cuota líquida del impuesto del 10 por 100 cuando las citadas contribuciones empresariales sean inferiores al 1,5 por 100 del salario bruto anual total en la entidad empleadora. | 2026-10-28 | transitional rule / computed case |
| 826 | The base / Ordinary social, commuting and environmental credits; LF270 | For example, assume a 2026 period, an employee aged 40, an established annual-gross-pay denominator of EUR 100,000 and EUR 1,000 of qualifying imputed employer contributions. | 831 | The base / Investment, research and employment; LF258 | Navarra declared-social-interest sponsorship credits are marginal 30% throughEUR 30,000,35% on the nextEUR 30,000 and 40% above EUR 60,000, with 40% on qualifying women-only sport sponsorship, recipient reporting and the gambling exclusion. Renewable-energy investment starts at 15%, with uplifts capped at 30%: ten points for zero-GHG electricity generation, ten for qualifying storage over2kWh, five for a microgrid with two renewable sources, five for shared self-consumption/energy communities; thermal hydraulic heating/hot-water connection adds five points and replacing gas with renewable hydrogen adds up to fifteen according to the qualifying use. Apply the mandatory-building-installation exclusions, special70%-of-cost mixed hot-water/heating rule and heat-pump renewable-share calculation, supported by the energy-authority report; new qualifying electric vehicles 30%, plug-in hybrids 5%, with category base capsEUR 35,000(M1/N1), EUR 5,000(L1e/L2e), EUR 10,000(L3e/L4e/L5e), EUR 15,000(L6e/L7e), EUR 150,000(N 2/N 3). Charging systems give 15%, plus five points for public access, two points for 7.4–22 kW or five points over 22 kW; the base ceilings are EUR 5,000 normal-power, EUR 25,000 high-power up to 50 kW and EUR 200,000 above 50 kW, supported by the energy-authority report. The excess over the relevant vehicle/charger base cap can qualify separately under art.58, avoiding duplicate base. The new 2026 decarbonisation credit is 15% of qualifying new tangible business investment achieving at least 30,000 kWh/year final-energy savings, less the amount received for transferring the energy savings; cap the credit at EUR 1.5m. Generation follows the resolution registering the energy-saving certificates, supported by the competent energy authority's report. Keep art.64 investments separately identified as fixed assets for five years or shorter useful life and apply the statutory leasing, retention and clawback conditions. Separate these from real-estate energy improvements and from the personal income-tax vehicle credit. [N arts.63–64.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-2356) | Navarra LF26/2016 article 64 | https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-2356#ar-64 | 4. El porcentaje de deducción establecido en el apartado 1 podrá incrementarse, sin que en ningún caso supere el 30 por 100, en los siguientes supuestos: | 2026-10-28 | rule |

Charging systems give 15%, plus five points for public access, two points for 7.4–22 kW or five points over 22 kW; the base ceilings are EUR 5,000 normal-power, EUR 25,000 high-power up to 50 kW and EUR 200,000 above 50 kW, supported by the energy-authority report. The excess over the relevant vehicle/charger base cap can qualify separately under art.58, avoiding duplicate base. The new 2026 decarbonisation credit is 15% of qualifying new tangible business investment achieving at least 30,000 kWh/year final-energy savings, less the amount received for transferring the energy savings; cap the credit at EUR 1.5m. Generation follows the resolution registering the energy-saving certificates, supported by the competent energy authority's report. Keep art.64 investments separately identified as fixed assets for five years or shorter useful life and apply the statutory leasing, retention and clawback conditions. Separate these from real-estate energy improvements and from the personal income-tax vehicle credit. | 27 | For 2026, the agreements use the EUR 12 million preceding-period operations threshold. Annualise operations for a short period and use estimated first-year operations until actual figures are known. Operations means VAT-exclusive consideration for business supplies, excluding the equivalence surcharge; it is not automatically accounting turnover or assets. At or below EUR 12 million, the ordinary single company pays the administration of its fiscal domicile. Above it, collection follows the current year's territorial operations, with the percentage rounded to two decimals. Calculate one company's taxable income under the selected governing law, then allocate its liability. Do not apply each territory's headline rate separately to its sales. [CE arts.14–18; CN arts.18–23.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Who this applies to; current LF28; exact retained |
| 29 | For a Basque-domiciled company, Basque law governs unless preceding operations exceed EUR 12 million and at least 75% took place in common territory. A common-territory company above EUR 12 million uses Basque law if at least 75% of preceding operations took place in the Basque Country; a common-domiciled fiscal-group member needs 100% there. Select the province under that province's art.2: domicile normally controls; if all Basque operations occurred outside the domicile province, use the sole operating province or the province with the larger share of the other two; a common-territory company coming into Basque law uses the province with the largest Basque operations share. Record all three provincial percentages, the common-territory percentage and preceding/current years separately. [CE art.14; B/A/G art.2.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Bizkaia NF11/2013](https://www.bizkaia.eus/documents/880307/15187815/ca_11_2013.pdf/5a463c1d-a59b-7e48-6429-80fd22f30bc6?t=1768908575887), [Álava NF37/2013](https://web.araba.eus/documents/d/araba/norma-foral-del-impuesto-sobre-sociedades_cas-3-pdf), [Gipuzkoa NF2/2014](https://www.gipuzkoa.eus/documents/2456431/8.0761374E7/NF%202-2014%20%282026%29.pdf/f1231a01-1f83-ee15-e569-7b9b84d44d54) | Who this applies to; current LF30; exact retained |
| 31 | For Navarra, exclusive Navarra collection entails Navarra law. A company paying both Navarra and the State uses domicile law, except a Navarra-domiciled company with at least 75% preceding operations in common territory uses common law; a common-domiciled company with at least 75% in Navarra uses Navarra law, with the art.18 fiscal-group exception. Keep a case involving both Navarra and one or more Basque provinces for a specific agreement analysis rather than treating Navarra as a fourth Basque province. [CN arts.18–19.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Who this applies to; current LF32; exact retained |
| 33 | Build the operations ledger from the statutory connecting factors: goods generally where made available or where dispatch starts; transformed goods at the final transformation; industrial installations use the preparation/manufacturing place if installation cost does not exceed 15%; electricity at generating plants; immovable supplies and related services where the property is; ordinary services where performed from. Agriculture/fishing products, transport and leasing transport equipment have domicile rules; allocate foreign operations proportionately to the remaining operations. Customer address alone does not supply this analysis. [CE art.16; CN arts.20–21.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Who this applies to; current LF34; exact retained |
| 35 | Advance payments use the last return's allocation, subject to the agreement's change-notification routes; deduct the instalment actually paid to each administration from its share. File with every administration entitled to collection. The governing law determines the instalment method even where another administration collects part of it. A State-law company allocating tax to a foral treasury must therefore retain State instalment calculations. [CE arts.17–18; CN arts.22–23.](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-9969), [Navarra Economic Agreement](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1990-31117) | Current LF36; own advance-tax collection/legislative separation and CN24 pointer retained. |

| 122 | The Basque equalisation reserve normally allows a deduction bounded by 10% of freely distributable accounting profit, 15% of the specified taxable base and a reserve balance of 25% of fiscal equity. | 124 | The Basque productive/business reserve in art.53 provides a separate local reserve/materialisation method. Álava's current rates are a 65%-of-dotations reduction capped at 45% of taxable base and a 50%-of-fiscal-equity reserve balance, with the three-year investment categories, double-investment requirement for new art.61 assets and prior approval for the specified participation route. **Not yet confirmed:** a controlling Álava special delegated measurement or contrary interpretation beyond the supplied own-law net-result worksheet, and its deferred-tax/current-credit/other-adjustment or incomparable-history populations; attribution or adjustment interactions outside the supplied reasoned ordinary ledgers and return-specific rounding; Gipuzkoa complementary-tax exception's precise paragraph scope for a large-group case; operational2027 forms beyond the supplied statutory windows and confirmed provincial232 triggers. Specialist culture/financing, IP nexus, reinvestment, patrimonial entities, fiscal groups, co-ops and restructuring require their own complete methods before use. The supplied B/G fully taxable incremental-profit method and Álava's labelled own-law net-result/current-tax interpretation each give a positive surcharge within their explicit input bounds; neither supplies every other accounting or tax-attribution branch.
